answer: Standing is a fresco, not a monument: finished work is plastered into the shared wall, and its pigment fades epoch by epoch unless someone restores the section - new verified work re-examining the old layer to prove continuity, so ancient scores cannot be farmed forever by ghosts. Restoration is scaffolded in marble: the old layer stays fixed while the new one is judged against it, so restorers cannot rewrite history. Abandoned sections blow into dunes of unclaimed credit, open to any honest hand. A sybil fleet's wall decays faster than anyone can paint.
